card.name: Lebang Boomani
card.tagline: Tripuri harvest dance mimicking the catching of lebang insects
card.profile: Lebang Boomani (Lebang Bumani) is a harvest folk dance of the Tripuri people, performed after the Garia Puja sowing season when colourful 'lebang' insects (green cicadas) visit the hill slopes in search of sown seeds (Wikipedia, Lebang Boomani dance; Tripura State Portal). Men set the rhythm with bamboo clappers called 'tokkas,' whose sound is believed to draw the insects from hiding, while women in groups run across the slopes to catch them; the dance is a stylised re-enactment of this activity (Adivasi Lives Matter; Tripura State Portal). It is accompanied by the bamboo flute, khamb, sarinda and bamboo cymbals, and women adorn themselves with silver chains and bronze ear and nose ornaments (Tripura State Portal).
card.insight: The number of insects caught is traditionally believed to foretell how good the harvest will be - embedding agrarian augury in the choreography and reflecting the deep cultural life that developed around jhum cultivation (Adivasi Lives Matter; Dances of Tripura).
card.image_significance: The insect-catching harvest dance. A representative image shows ornate costume and expressive hand-gesture (mudra) detail — Tripura (Tripuri), India.
